name: Fidelity Jones
label: Dischord
lede: Two Beefeater refugees and their housemates spent two years trying to push punk somewhere stranger, quit in 1990, and came back thirty-three years later because a podcast got them talking about cover songs.

eras.title: The band in the group house
eras.text: Beefeater had been the D.C. band that brought funk and jazz into Revolution Summer. When it ended, singer Tomas Squip and bassist Dug E. Bird didn't go far: they started over with the people they lived with, at the Positive Force house, a group home for the scene's activist collective.

years.h: Fidelity Jones forms in the Positive Force house
years.p: After Beefeater breaks up, [[Tomas Squip|273702be-180d-487a-9238-2154aea60b92]] and Dug E. Bird start Fidelity Jones with two of their housemates at the Positive Force house, Maria Jones and drummer [[Jerry Busher|59c39d46-efd2-4fa0-912e-93ead7a4ab97]].

years.h: Maria Jones leaves Fidelity Jones for Holy Rollers
years.p: After recording two songs with the original line-up, Maria Jones leaves Fidelity Jones to play drums in [[Holy Rollers|d8e0e0b1-8cd9-40c7-b413-71cfcaa90547]].

eras.title: Pushing the envelope
eras.text: Dischord's own history says Fidelity Jones kept pushing the musical envelope of punk in a hard stretch for the scene, and got to the eclectic sound they'd been after from the start. The proof is the Piltdown Lad EP and the Venus on Lovely single, then the band called it in spring 1990.

years.h: Andy Charneco brings the D.C. underground with him
years.p: Andy Charneco joins Fidelity Jones on guitar, with a résumé from the city's stranger corners: White Boy and On Beyond Zebra.

years.h: State of the Union comes out with Fidelity Jones' first songs
years.p: Fidelity Jones' original four, with Maria Jones, recorded Pilate and Blood Stone Burn in 1988 for this Dischord benefit compilation. Dischord 032 finally appears in 1989 alongside [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]], [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]] and [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]].
Fidelity Jones' debut EP: six songs cut at Inner Ear, the production credited to "Andy & Fidelity Jones."
Two songs, Venus on Lovely and Destructor, recorded at Bias Studios rather than Inner Ear. It's Fidelity Jones' last release until Magdeburg Lad in 2024.
Dischord dates Fidelity Jones from spring 1988 to spring 1990: two years almost to the season.

eras.title: The drummer's long road, and a podcast
eras.text: Drummer Jerry Busher went furthest, from the Positive Force house to Fugazi's stage. Then, after three decades apart, a podcast interview put Fidelity Jones' last line-up back in a room.

years.h: Jerry Busher, from Fugazi's crew to Fugazi's records
years.p: Jerry Busher, a Fugazi roadie through the '90s, ends up playing extra drums, percussion and trumpet with Fugazi live, and appears on The Argument and Furniture. The same year he starts [[French Toast|f9e0402f-c675-46d9-985f-07001bba6480]].
years.xp: Busher kept going: [[Deathfix|db0e5c06-c091-46d4-bd42-5ba2ee299123]] from 2013, and drums and percussion with [[Scream|b9f52132-28af-4cea-9558-165cd125f9b7]] in 2023 and 2024, per Wikipedia. His list of bands also runs through [[The Evens|3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8]], [[Beauty Pill|976b28a1-dd68-4c43-ba08-ba15b58963b2]] and [[Blonde Redhead|6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219]].

years.h: Magdeburg Lad: a podcast chat becomes a comeback EP
years.p: A 2023 podcast interview reunited Tomas Squip, Dug E. Bird, Jerry Busher and Andy Charneco, and talk of their old live covers turned into a studio booking. The digital-only EP, Dischord 198.5, followed in April 2024.
years.xp:
Two years in the making, it has two covers, one old original they never recorded, and one new song, JOY. The title echoes their 1989 debut EP, Piltdown Lad.

The band says it isn't a one-off. Fidelity Jones, per its Bandcamp and Dischord's announcement, will remain an ongoing recording entity with more music planned.
